description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of various models—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—across different co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^1$ to $10^3$, and the y-axis showing accuracy from 60% to 85%. Each model is represented by a distinct line: Base (black, solid line with circles), FT (blue, dashed line with triangles), IKE (red, dashed line with triangles), MEND (brown, solid line with diamonds), MEMIT (purple, dashed line with diamonds), and ROME (green, solid line with squares). The Base model starts at approximately 63% accuracy and increases to around 77% as the co-occurrence number grows. The FT model begins at about 64% and rises to roughly 79%. The IKE model starts at approximately 66% and reaches around 81%. The MEND model starts at about 68% and increases to around 82%. The MEMIT model begins at approximately 68% and climbs to about 83%. The ROME model starts at around 74% and increases to approximately 84%. All models show a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy across the range.
